articles.title: Silent shareholders hold the key to Tata Motors' Iveco deal
Tata Motors CV Q2 Results Preview: Profit may rise up to 44% YoY, revenue 45%; margins, volume growth in focus
Tata Motors pips Mahindra to be No. 2 car company in April-September
Iveco Group shareholders approve Tata Motors' takeover proposals
Iveco shareholders approve Tata Motors' takeover bid; acceptance threshold cut to 80 pc

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors must win support from roughly three‑quarters of Iveco’s silent shareholders to meet the 80 % acceptance needed for its €3.9 billion acquisition; about 52.9 % of shares backed the deal, the offer was sweetened to €14.40 per share, and the combined entity would generate about €21 billion in revenue.

For Q2 FY27 Tata Motors’ commercial‑vehicle arm is projected to post volume growth of about 43 % YoY, revenue of Rs 24,218.4‑24,638.1 crore (≈44 % YoY), and adjusted PAT growth estimates of 44.3 % (JM Financial) versus 25.7 % (MOFSL); margins face pressure despite a 2.5 % price hike, with LCV volumes up 53.1 % YoY.

Tata Motors overtook Mahindra & Mahindra to become India’s second‑largest passenger‑vehicle maker in April‑Sept FY27, dispatching over 3.9 lakh units (up 43 % YoY) versus Mahindra’s just under 3.6 lakh (up ~20 %); overall domestic passenger‑vehicle dispatches rose 28.3 % to around 26.4 lakh units.

Iveco Group shareholders approved all resolutions tied to Tata Motors’ €3.91 billion takeover, lowering the minimum acceptance threshold from 95 % to 80 %, endorsing the €14.40 per‑share offer and authorising post‑offer demerger, delisting and board appointments; the tender offer is set to close on 26 Oct 2026.

Iveco shareholders ratified Tata Motors’ takeover bid, cutting the acceptance threshold to 80 % and confirming the €14.40 per‑share price; the deal was initially valued at around €3.8 billion (≈Rs 38,240 crore) with earlier valuation at €3.82 billion, and includes amendments for delisting, board changes and a possible post‑offer demerger.

key_points.text: Tata Motors needs to secure support from silent shareholders to achieve the 80 % acceptance threshold for its €3.9 billion Iveco acquisition, with the offer price now €14.40 per share and the combined business expected to generate about €21 billion in annual revenue.

Iveco shareholders approved the takeover proposals, lowering the minimum acceptance level to 80 % and confirming the €14.40 per‑share offer; the transaction is valued at €3.91 billion according to the announcement, while another source cites a valuation of around €3.8 billion, indicating a discrepancy in reported deal size.

Tata Motors’ commercial‑vehicle division is expected to deliver ~43 % YoY volume growth in Q2 FY27, with revenue rising about 44 % YoY to Rs 24,218.4‑24,638.1 crore and adjusted PAT growth estimates ranging from 25.7 % to 44.3 %; margins remain under pressure due to input‑cost inflation despite a 2.5 % price hike.

Tata Motors became India’s second‑largest passenger‑vehicle manufacturer in April‑Sept FY27, posting domestic dispatches of over 3.9 lakh units (up 43 % YoY) and overtaking Mahindra, which dispatched just under 3.6 lakh units (up ~20 %).

industry_context.text: The Indian passenger‑vehicle market recorded robust growth of 28.3 % YoY in April‑Sept FY27, driven by strong demand for SUVs and electric vehicles, with Mahindra’s BE and XEV models surging 82 %.
The commercial‑vehicle sector is seeing consolidation as Tata Motors’ acquisition of Iveco aims to expand its global footprint and product portfolio, particularly in Europe.
Rising input‑cost inflation and pricing pressures are key factors affecting commercial‑vehicle margins across the industry, as highlighted in earnings previews.

Tata Motors CV Q2 Results Preview: Profit may rise up to 44% YoY, revenue 45%; margins, volume growth in focus
Tata Motors pips Mahindra to be No. 2 car company in April-September
Iveco Group shareholders approve Tata Motors' takeover proposals
Iveco shareholders approve Tata Motors' takeover bid; acceptance threshold cut to 80 pc

article_briefs.brief: Tata Motors must win over most of Iveco’s silent shareholders—roughly three in four investors who stayed away from Friday’s special shareholder meeting—to complete its €3.9 billion acquisition and delist the Italian truck maker, as it still needs the 80 % shareholder acceptance required for full control. While shareholders holding about 52.9 % of Iveco’s common shares, including promoter Exor with 27 %, backed the deal‑related resolutions, Tata must persuade shareholders owning about 27 % of common shares from among those who did not vote, after about one in three non‑promoter votes were cast against the resolutions and 37.27 million votes (about 13.7 % of 271.2 million common shares) opposed the appointment of Natarajan Chandrasekaran. The offer was sweetened by 2 % from €14.10 per share to €14.40 on 9 October, and if Tata reaches the 66.67 % threshold but falls short of 80 %, it can waive the higher threshold but would be unable to delist Iveco or implement the planned de‑merger, leaving a combined business projected to generate annual revenue of about €21 billion and sales of over 590,000 vehicles.

Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles is expected to post Q2FY27 profit growth of up to 44% YoY and revenue growth of around 44‑45% YoY, driven by a volume increase of roughly 43% YoY. JM Financial projects revenue of Rs 24,218.4 crore (up 43.6% YoY and 25.3% QoQ) with adjusted PAT up 44.3%, while Motilal Oswal forecasts revenue of Rs 24,638.1 crore (up 45.4% YoY) and adjusted PAT up 25.7%; volume estimates are 1,35,114 units (up 42.7% YoY, 24.5% QoQ) and 1,37,339 units (up 43% YoY, 26.3% sequentially), with LCVs up 53.1% YoY and MHCVs up 31%. Margins remain under pressure despite a net price hike of 2.5% since July, with JM Financial seeing sequential EBITDA margin improvement and Motilal Oswal anticipating a sharper decline.

Tata Motors overtook Mahindra & Mahindra to become India's second‑largest passenger‑vehicle manufacturer by domestic dispatches in the April‑Sept 2026 period (first half of FY27). Tata's domestic passenger‑vehicle dispatches surged 43% to over 3.9 lakh units, while Mahindra posted just under 3.6 lakh units, a growth of around 20% (Maruti Suzuki retained the lead). Mahindra's BE and XEV models jumped 82% to 42,338 units, raising their contribution from 7.8% to 11.8%, whereas Tata benefited from a 59% surge in utility‑vehicle dispatches and the broader industry grew 28.3% to around 26.4 lakh units.

Iveco Group shareholders approved all resolutions at an extraordinary general meeting in Amsterdam, lowering the minimum share acceptance threshold from 95 per cent to 80 per cent and clearing a key hurdle for Tata Motors’ proposed €3.91 billion acquisition, which remains subject to other conditions. Tata Motors, through its subsidiary TML CV Holdings, raised its offer price on October 9 to €14.40 per share and the tender offer is scheduled to close on October 26, unless extended, with the deal expected to strengthen Tata Motors’ global commercial‑vehicle position.

Iveco shareholders voted at an extraordinary general meeting in Amsterdam to approve all board‑proposed resolutions linked to Tata Motors' voluntary public tender offer, including lowering the minimum acceptance threshold from 95 per cent to 80 per cent of Iveco’s common shares. Tata Motors had raised its offer price by EUR 0.30 per share to EUR 14.40 (from EUR 14.10) and targets an acquisition value of around EUR 3.8 billion (nearly Rs 38,240 crore), previously valued at approximately EUR 3.82 billion. The tender offer acceptance period runs from September 7 to October 26, 2026, and the approved resolutions also cover amendments to the articles, board appointments and a possible post‑offer demerger contingent on meeting the 80 per cent ownership condition.

key_points.text: Tata Motors must persuade silent shareholders owning about 27 % of Iveco’s common shares to reach the 80 % acceptance threshold, after shareholders holding about 52.9 % supported the deal and 13.7 % of shares (37.27 million votes) opposed the appointment of Natarajan Chandrasekaran.

Iveco Group shareholders approved lowering the minimum acceptance threshold to 80 % and cleared a key hurdle for Tata Motors’ proposed €3.91 billion acquisition; the offer price was raised to €14.40 per share and the tender is scheduled to close on October 26, 2026, strengthening Tata Motors’ global commercial‑vehicle position.
The acquisition value is reported as €3.91 billion in one brief and as around €3.8 billion (nearly Rs 38,240 crore) in another, indicating a slight discrepancy in the announced deal size.

Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles is projected to post Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 24,218.4 crore (up 43.6 % YoY) and Rs 24,638.1 crore (up 45.4 % YoY) with adjusted PAT growth of 44.3 % and 25.7 % respectively; volume is expected around 1,35,114‑1,37,339 units, with LCVs up 53.1 % YoY and MHCVs up 31 %; margins remain under pressure despite a net price hike of 2.5 % since July.

Tata Motors overtook Mahindra & Mahindra to become India’s second‑largest passenger‑vehicle maker in the April‑Sept 2026 period, with domestic passenger‑vehicle dispatches surging 43 % to over 3.9 lakh units and utility‑vehicle dispatches up 59 %, while the broader industry grew 28.3 % to around 26.4 lakh units.

industry_context.text: The Indian automotive market expanded 28.3 % in the April‑Sept 2026 period, driven by strong utility‑vehicle demand and a rapid rise in electric‑vehicle models, exemplified by Mahindra’s BE and XEV models jumping 82 % to 42,338 units, signaling competitive pressures and a shift toward electrification.

The commercial‑vehicle sector faces margin pressure despite a net price increase of 2.5 % since July, with EBITDA margins expected to improve sequentially at one forecast but to decline at another, reflecting broader pricing and cost dynamics.
